title: Looking for some honest feedback
author: Ok-Cellist-8458
selftext:
I added the Commercial Self Promotion flair but what I really want is feedback on my game project.    
  
I started this project last year because I felt music games might be easier to stand out in short form videos. I've seen rhythm games catch my attention when scrolling. I'm an experienced game developer but not an artist or musician.  I can't pay for any assets so I knew I was gonna leverage AI where I can but still put my taste on visual and audio effects. Despite the potential AI backlash, it has been so fun to flex my creativity using Suno to fine tune music. The art direction I settled on vector graphics inspired by Geometry Wars because its easier for me to tune as an engineer. I've tested using my own blender models and animations and it just didn't look/feel as good to me.  And it would have been super expensive to get professional help in that direction.   
When I play my own game, I genuinely feel the signal of it being a fun game. Hitting and dashing on beat to music definitely gives off dopamine rushes. I don't know a lot of people but the small handful of people I had try it liked it as well.  I envision the game like people finger drumming to the beat of the their favorite songs and it definitely feels like that to me when I play on keyboard.   
The demo has one Jukebox slot where you can import your own MP3 — it analyzes it locally and builds the fight around it. That's the beat detection I'm most unsure about.  
  
I would definitely appreciate some feedback on the gameplay. Is it fun? Is it too hard and unforgiving with the beat detection? Is the vector graphics just not the direction to go? Is the tutorial still confusing? 

Thank you!
